words: حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage cites 10:22 as a parallel, but says its shift is expressed through two words and two states, unlike the one-word case under discussion.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم

rows.speaker: ابن الشجري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shajari distinguishes truthful negation (nafy) from denial known to be false (jahd); nafy is broader, so every jahd is nafy but not vice versa.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشجري ان كان النافي صادقا فيما قاله سمي كلامه نفيا وان كان يعلم كذب ما نفاه كان جحدا

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars do not distinguish nafy from jahd; the author prefers Ibn al-Shajari’s distinction.
rows.anchor: قال ومن العلماء من لايفرق بينهما والاصل ماذكرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negation is half of all speech, since speech is either affirmation or negation.
rows.anchor: هو شطر الكلام كله لان الكلام اما اثبات أو نفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that sound negation requires the negated attribute to be possible, and the Hanafi inference that prohibition therefore entails validity; negation can deny rational impossibility or a possible event that does not occur.
rows.anchor: والصواب ان انتفاء الشيء عن الشيء قد يكون لكونه لا يمكن منه عقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negated element is what immediately follows the negation particle: ما ضربت زيدا denies the act, while ما أنا ضربته denies that I was its agent.
rows.anchor: المنفي ما ولى حرف النفي فاذا قلت ماضربت زيدا كنت نافيا للفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The minimum six-month pregnancy is apt in a passage recalling hardship: a child born then rarely survives, so every addressee bears that burden; weaning has no comparable minimum, so its usual duration is named.
rows.anchor: لأن هذه المدة أقل مدة الحمل ولما كان الولد لا يعيش غالبا إذا وضع لستة أشهر كانت مشقة الحمل في هذه المدة موجودة لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exegete must know legal theory because it is among the greatest means of deriving rulings from Qur’anic verses.
rows.anchor: ولا بد من معرفة قواعد أصول الفقه فإنه من أعظم الطرق في استثمار الأحكام من الآيات

words: فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite noun in a negative context is general, as in the denial that God wrongs anyone and that any soul knows the hidden reward.
rows.anchor: فيستفاد عموم النكرة في سياق النفي من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite noun in an interrogative context is general: هل تعلم له سميا asks whether there is any namesake for God.
rows.anchor: وفي الإستفهام من قوله ﴿ هل تعلم له سميا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite noun under a conditional particle is general, as shown by the examples of seeing any person and any polytheist seeking protection.
rows.anchor: وفي الشرط من قوله ﴿ فإما ترين من البشر أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite noun under a prohibition is general; the command that no one turn back covers everyone addressed.
rows.anchor: وفي النهي من قوله ﴿ ولا يلتفت منكم أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In affirmative contexts, an indefinite singular can have a generalized individual reading; adding كل makes the generality explicit, as in كل نفس.
rows.anchor: وفي سياق الإثبات بعموم القلة المقتضى

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: In the Qur’anic expression of what God places within a soul’s capacity, the exception إلا ما آتاها refers to provision, not work.
rows.anchor: انتهى ما ذكره ابن فارس

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris says ya’s in the Qur’an usually means despair, except here, where it means know; he cites a poem his father recited as evidence.
rows.anchor: أفلم ييأس الذين آمنوا ﴾ أى ألم يعلموا قال ابن فارس

rows.speaker: الصاغاني
rows.claim: Al-Saghani attributes the cited poetic line to Suhaym ibn Wathil al-Yarbu‘i, while Ibn Faris reports it from his father.
rows.anchor: قال الصاغانى البيت لسحيم بن وثيل اليربوعى

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Qur’anic references to patience are generally commendatory, except these passages where the unbelievers’ endurance in clinging to idols is condemned.
rows.anchor: انتهى ما ذكره ابن فارس

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Other authorities say لعل usually means ‘so that,’ but in this verse it means ‘as though,’ describing the people as if immortal.
rows.anchor: وزاد غيره كل شىء فى القرآن لعلكم

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Other authorities distinguish the forms: أقسطوا means act justly, while القاسطون here are described as those who set another equal to God; the triliteral and quadriliteral roots differ.
rows.anchor: وكل شيء فى القرآن أقسطوا فهو بمعنى العدل

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Other authorities say كسف generally means a side or piece of the sky, but here in Surat al-Rum it means cloud fragments.
rows.anchor: وكل كسف فى القرآن يعنى جانبا من السماء

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: ماء معين generally means running water, but in Surat al-Mulk it means pure water accessible to buckets, identified here as Zamzam.
rows.anchor: وكل ماء معين فالمراد به الماء الجارى

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: لئلا generally means ‘so that not,’ but in this verse it means ‘so that the People of the Book may know.’
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن لئلا فهو بمعنى كيلا

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Darkness and light in the Qur’an generally signify unbelief and faith; this verse is the exception, referring to night and day.
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن من الظلمات إلى النور

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: صوم generally means the known fast, but Mary’s vow in this verse means silence.
rows.anchor: وكل صوم فى القرآن فهو الصيام المعروف

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
rows.claim: Al-Dani explains حاضرة البحر as ‘in sight’; the form with ظ in المحتظر means enclosure or restraint and occurs only once with that sense.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو عمرو الدانى فى قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza can precede the conditional particle إن; هل cannot occupy that position.
rows.anchor: ولا تقول هل إن تخرج اخرج معك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza may be omitted, as in وتلك نعمة تمنها علي; other examples are هذا ربي under one interpretation and Ibn Muḥaysin’s reading سواء عليهم ءأنذرتهم.
rows.anchor: ومنها جواز حذفها كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن الطراوة
rows.claim: Ibn al-Tarawa claims the hamza is always balanced by an expressed or understood alternative; the author reports al-Saffar’s objection that every interrogative asks for certainty and hamza examples with alternatives are abundant.
rows.anchor: زعم ابن الطراوة انها لاتكون ابدا الا معادلة

rows.speaker: الصفار
rows.claim: Al-Saffar rejects Ibn al-Tarawa’s restriction: هل قام زيد also asks whether he stood or not, and hamza questions without an expressed alternative are common.
rows.anchor: ورد عليه الصفار وقال لا فرق بينها وبين غيرها فإنك اذا قلت هل قام زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza precedes conjunctions and other interrogative particles because it is the original question particle and has initial position; conjunctions otherwise cannot precede part of an interrogative clause.
rows.anchor: وانما خولف هذا في الهمزة لانها اصل ادوات الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هل is more explicitly restricted to verbs than the hamza; nominal clauses after هل emphasize that the requested qualities are present and established, unlike verbal forms that suggest renewal.
rows.anchor: وهل أظهر في الاختصاص بالفعل من الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza can move beyond its basic interrogative use to convey denial, affirmation, report, and other meanings discussed under interrogation.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه يعدل بالهمزة عن أصلها فيتجوز بها عن النفي والإيجاب والتقرير وغير ذلك المعاني السالفة في بحث الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When hamza precedes رأيت, the verb no longer means seeing with eye or mind; it means ‘tell me,’ semantically takes a preposition, but grammatically takes a direct object.
rows.anchor: وإذا دخلت على رأيت امتنع إن تكون من رؤية البصر أو القلب وصارت بمعنى أخبرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza before لم conveys either reminder or astonishment at something momentous; in either case the construction warns the hearer.
rows.anchor: وإذا دخلت على لم أفادت معنيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أم is a connective substituting for repetition of a noun or verb; grammarians variously analyze it as connective, interrogative connective, or أو with a changed consonant. It divides into connected and disconnected forms; the connected form asks for identification, follows a hamza, and has one clause on both sides.
rows.anchor: أم حرف عطف نائب عن تكرير الاسم والفعل

words: أَطَّلَعَ ٱلْغَيْبَ أَمِ ٱتَّخَذَ عِندَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَهْدًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا is the opposite of affirmative إي when used as a rejection, as in the response to the boast that the unbeliever has access to the unseen or a covenant.
rows.anchor: وهي نقيض إي في الإثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In other settings كلا can mean حقا and serve as an oath adjunct, as in كلا والقمر; it may also introduce confirmations about judgment and the records of deeds.
rows.anchor: وتكون بمعنى حقا صلة لليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The كلا after the claim that wealth made its owner immortal can mean either a rebuke or an affirmation.
rows.anchor: يحسب أن ماله أخلده كلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ over pausing around كلا: some pause on it as rebuke, others begin with it as confirmation; the author prefers pausing when it rebukes and beginning with it when it confirms.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من نظر إلى المعنيين فيقف عليها إذا كانت بمعنى الردع

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret ذلك and هذا as opposites of negation, and كذلك as an opposite of كلا, meaning ‘that is how it was done’; the author cites the following conjunction as evidence of an implied preceding clause.
rows.anchor: ونقل ابن فارس عن بعضهم

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, al-Akhfash, al-Mubarrad, and al-Zajjaj explain كلا meaning لا as rejecting an elided clause, approximately ليس الأمر كذلك; it is used at a pause for rebuke, denial, or rejection.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب الخليل وسيبويه والأخفش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because كلا carries threat and warning, it appears only in Meccan suras; the author says a sura containing it should therefore be recognized as Meccan.
rows.anchor: ولذلك لم تقع في القرآن إلا في سورة مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first class of Qur’anic كلا permits both pausing before it and beginning after it, depending on whether it is read as rebuke or confirmation; twelve examples are listed, including these four.
rows.anchor: إحداها ما يجوز الوقف عليه والابتداء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second class has three instances where كلا is neither a stopping point nor a place to begin; the source lists two in al-Shu‘ara and one in Saba.
rows.anchor: والثانى ثلاثة أحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third class has eighteen instances where one begins with كلا but does not pause before it; the listed cases occupy fifteen suras, all in the latter half of the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: والثالث ثمانية عشر حرفا

rows.speaker: عبد العزيز الديريني
rows.claim: Al-Dayrini’s verse mnemonic says كلا never descended in Yathrib and never appears in the upper half of the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وللشيخ عبد العزيز الديرينى رحمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word recurs in the latter half because most of it was revealed in Mecca, where tyrants were numerous and threats, reproaches, and denunciations were needed; the Jews in the first half were weak and humiliated.
rows.anchor: وحكمة ذلك أن النصف الآخر نزل أكثره بمكة

words: إِن كُلُّ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّآ ءَاتِى ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَبْدًۭا
rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali and others, followed by al-Razi, give five hundred as the number of legal verses; the author says they likely mean explicit rulings, since stories and parables also yield many rulings, and directs readers to Ibn Abd al-Salam.
rows.anchor: ثم قيل إن آيات الأحكام خمسمائة آية وهذا ذكره الغزالي وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legal verses divide into explicit rulings and rulings derived by inference; derived rulings in turn come either from one verse alone or by joining multiple verses.
rows.anchor: ثم هو قسمان أحدهما ما صرح به في الأحكام

words: إلا على أزواجهم أو ما ملكت أيمانهم
فمن ابتغى وراء ذلك فأولئك هم العادون
rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi‘i infers that masturbation is prohibited from the exception limiting sexual relations to spouses and those lawfully possessed, and the condemnation of seeking beyond that.
rows.anchor: كاستنباط الشافعي تحريم الاستمناء باليد

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi‘i infers the validity of non-Muslims’ marriages from the Qur’an’s references to Pharaoh’s wife and Abu Lahab’s wife.
rows.anchor: واستنباط صحة أنكحة الكفار من قوله تعالى

words: إِن كُلُّ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّآ ءَاتِى ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَبْدًۭا
rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi‘i infers that ownership automatically frees an ascendant or descendant: servitude is placed opposite parentage, so the two statuses cannot coexist.
rows.anchor: واستنباطه عتق الأصل والفرع بمجرد الملك

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi‘i takes the warning against following a path other than the believers’ path as proof that consensus is authoritative.
rows.anchor: واستنباطه حجية الإجماع من قوله

words: حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الأبيض من الخيط الأسود من الفجر
rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi‘i infers that a person may fast while in major ritual impurity: intercourse is allowed throughout the night, so the required bath may be delayed until daytime.
rows.anchor: صحة صوم الجنب من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ali and Ibn Abbas infer that the minimum pregnancy is six months by combining the thirty-month term for pregnancy and weaning with the two-year weaning term; al-Shafi‘i adopts this inference.
rows.anchor: كاستنباط علي وابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa infers a maximum nursing period of thirty months: the full stated term can apply to each of two matters, and the added period beyond two years is assigned to nursing because pregnancy is shorter and children transition to other food.
rows.anchor: واحتج بها أبو حنيفة على أن أكثر الرضاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With من understood as a relative pronoun, the verse combines agreement with كل’s singular form and plural meaning; if من is an indefinite descriptor, the example belongs to the prior category.
rows.anchor: وقد اجتمع مراعاة اللفظ والمعنى في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When كل is cut off from an expressed genitive, it can agree either with its singular form or its collective meaning; the source gives both singular and plural examples.
rows.anchor: الثالث إن تقطع عن الإضافة لفظا فيجوز مراعاة لفظها ومراعاة معناها

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: Abu al-Fath explains mixed singular and plural agreement by the word’s singular form and collective meaning, with an omitted plural genitive sometimes reflected in agreement and sometimes not.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الفتح وعلته إن أحد الجمعين عندهم كان عن صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative analysis estimates a singular omitted noun where the predicate is singular and a plural noun where it is plural; both estimates still convey a collective meaning.
rows.anchor: قيل ولو قال قائل حيث أفرد يقدر الحذف مفردا وحيث جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural verb in كل في فلك يسبحون cannot describe each sun, moon, night, or day as a plural; al-Zamakhshari’s estimate كل أحد in a related example supports the analysis.
rows.anchor: إن كلا من الشمس والقمر والليل والنهار لايصح وصفه بالجمع

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli says a detached كل should take a plural predicate because it means a group; for the cited singular predicates, he invokes contextual clues favoring that wording.
rows.anchor: وقال السهيلي السهيلي في نتاج الفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir is the knowledge of understanding God’s revealed Book, explaining its meanings, and deriving its rulings and wisdom; it draws on language, grammar, morphology, rhetoric, legal theory, and readings, and requires knowledge of revelation contexts and abrogation.
rows.anchor: التفسير علم يعرف به فهم كتاب الله المنزل على نبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetical works reflect their authors’ strongest fields: al-Zajjaj and al-Wahidi emphasize rare vocabulary, al-Tha‘labi stories, al-Zamakhshari rhetoric, and Fakhr al-Din kalam and rational disciplines.
rows.anchor: فالزجاج والواحدى في البسيط يغلب عليهما الغريب والثعلبى يغلب عليه القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God addressed people in a language they understand and revealed each book in its people’s language, commentary is needed when concise expression hides subtle meaning, premises are omitted, wording permits several readings, or a human text contains errors or omissions.
rows.anchor: وإنما احتيج إلى الشروح لأمور ثلاثة أحدها كمال فضيلة المصنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an came in clear Arabic among the most eloquent Arabs; they knew its surface meanings and rulings, while subtler meanings emerged through study and, often, questions to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: إن القرآن إنما أنزل بلسان عربى مبين في زمن أفصح العرب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When the Companions asked which of them had not wronged himself, the Prophet explained ظلم in this verse as associating partners with God and cited Luqman’s description of shirk as a great wrong.
rows.anchor: فسره النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم بالشرك

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha asked the Prophet about the easy reckoning; he said it is the presentation of the account, while the person whose account is examined in detail is punished.
rows.anchor: وكسؤال عائشة رضى الله عنها عن الحساب اليسير

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: The source also cites Adi ibn Hatim’s question about the thread he placed under his pillow as an example of Companions asking the Prophet about a verse’s intended meaning.
rows.anchor: وكقصة عدى ابن حاتم فى الخيط الذى وضعه

words: ولن يؤخر الله نفسا إذا جاء أجلها
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some infer the Prophet’s lifespan of sixty-three from the verse at the head of the sixty-third sura and the following sura al-Taghabun, which signifies loss at his death.
rows.anchor: استنبط عمر النبى صالى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source notes an inference that Jesus’ speech from قال إني عبد الله to أبعث حيا has thirty-three words, matching an inferred lifespan of thirty-three years.
rows.anchor: ثلاث وثلاثون كلمة وعمره ثلاث وثلاثون سنة

rows.speaker: الناس
rows.claim: Some inferred an earthquake in 702 AH from the abjad values of alif and dhal in the opening of Surat al-Zalzalah.
rows.anchor: وقد استنبط الناس زلزلة عام اثنين وسبعمائة

rows.speaker: بعض أئمة العرب
rows.claim: Some Arab scholars used abjad calculation on the opening of Surat al-Rum to infer Jerusalem’s capture and recovery from enemy hands.
rows.anchor: استنبط بعض أئمة العرب فتح بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha‘bi explains the omission of paternal and maternal uncles from the listed exceptions: they might leave a woman with a son who is not her mahram, creating temptation; the author says this rationale is vulnerable because similar risk applies to named categories.
rows.anchor: وقد سئل الشعبى عن ذلك فقال لئلا يضعه العم عند ابنه

words: ولا على أنفسكم أن تأكلوا من بيوتكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain the omission of children from the verse permitting eating in relatives’ homes by saying children are included in the phrase بيوتكم.
rows.anchor: ولا على أنفسكم أن تأكلوا من بيوتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage’s tenth rhetorical mode is a metonymy that conveys the gist of a sentence whose apparent wording is not intended literally, without assigning each word a literal or figurative sense.
rows.anchor: عاشرها ان يعمد إلى جملة ورد معناها على خلاف الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews’ claim that God’s hand is tied is hyperbolic reproach; the passage says it followed their denial of the Prophet and God’s withholding of gifts from a wealthy group.
rows.anchor: سابعها قصد المبالغة في التشنيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response غلت أيديهم is read as a matching figurative curse, or literally as their hands being fettered in captivity and punishment; the source also calls them exceedingly miserly.
rows.anchor: فيحمل على المجاز على وجه الدعاء والمطابقة للفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بل يداه مبسوطتان is a metonym for generosity; the dual form, although the earlier phrase is singular, intensifies the sense of openhandedness.
rows.anchor: كناية عن كرمه وثنى اليد وان افردت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording draws attention to Abu Lahab’s destination: his end is the Fire of the Flame.
rows.anchor: ثامنها التنبيه على مصيره كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حمالة الحطب means a slanderer and also points to the woman’s final destination as fuel for Hell.
rows.anchor: أي نمامة ومصيرها إلى ان تكون حطبا لجهنم

words: ولو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A concise verb can stand for several actions; in فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا the omitted actions are producing a sura like the Qur’an, which they will never produce.
rows.anchor: تاسعها قصد الاختصار ومنه الكناية عن افعال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats الاستواء على العرش as a metonym for sovereignty, since sitting on a throne occurs only with kingship.
rows.anchor: وهذه الكناية استنبطها الزمخشري وخرج عليها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari’s method reads the earth’s being in God’s grasp as a metonym for majesty and grandeur, without construing grasp and right hand literally or figuratively as separate terms.
rows.anchor: الآية انه كناية عن عظمته وجلالته

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi objects that this broad metonymic method opens the door to esoteric reinterpretations, such as reading Moses’ command to remove his shoes as total devotion rather than an actual command about shoes.
rows.anchor: وقد اعترض الامام فخر الدين على ذلك
